children: What happened?

A number of stocks fell in the afternoon session after AI-linked shares continued to pull back. Anthropic slid more than 10% following its debut, failing to revive confidence in the sector's spending boom.

Investors had looked to Anthropic's record $81.3 billion initial public offering and Nvidia's quarterly earnings beat under interim CEO Colette Kress to steady sentiment following Jensen Huang's resignation, CNBC reported. Instead, Anthropic's retreat toward its $83 offer price echoed Seaport Research warnings, covered by CNBC, that its valuation demands much faster revenue growth.

Separately, Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook warned against delaying rate hikes ahead of an expected December increase. Compounding the concerns, President Donald Trump threatened penalties on overseas U.S. data-center builds as new Commerce Department export-licensing rules weighed on chipmakers.
The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks.
Among others, the following stocks were impacted:

Zooming in on DigitalOcean

DigitalOcean’s shares are extremely volatile and have had 75 moves greater than 5% over the last year. But moves this big are rare even for DigitalOcean and indicate this news significantly impacted the market’s perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 4 days ago when the stock dropped 6.8% on the news that investor concerns intensified over the longevity of the artificial intelligence rally as the Federal Reserve issued warnings over artificial intelligence debt.

Fed Governor Michael S. Barr noted in a speech that on-balance-sheet debt at the seven largest AI firms is expected to top $800 billion by year-end while nominal off-balance-sheet leases and guarantees exceed $3 trillion. Anthropic's anticipated IPO and Nvidia's earnings results later in the week could test capital flows and AI unit economics. When major artificial intelligence leaders face selling pressure, the momentum often spills over into peer semiconductor and software companies across the United States equity market.

Separately, CNBC reported Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security will require licenses for advanced chips bound for Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, and Brazil to block Chinese firms from leasing Nvidia compute abroad. That policy shift could complicate Wall Street's AI deal pipeline.

DigitalOcean is up 36.3% since the beginning of the year, but at $66.74 per share, it is still trading 63.2% below its 52-week high of $181.29 from June 2026. Despite the year-to-date gain, investors who bought $1,000 worth of DigitalOcean’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at only $649.14.
